newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley new chief faces challenges.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley new chief faces challenges.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co's newly appointed chief executive officer, William Davis, faces a raft of challenges in trying to turn around the printing company, analysts said on Wednesday.

"Donnelley has been struggling in recent years," Merrill Lynch analyst Robert Curran said. "It needs to be better focused, better cost-positioned and organized so it's more responsive to what its customers want, rather than what it thinks the customers want."
Curran said Davis "seems to have the qualifications that mesh well with Donnelley, namely experience in turnaround situations in mature industries. He also has had marketing experience."

Donnelley said Davis, as senior executive vice president of Emerson Electric Co, was largely responsible for bringing that company's Skil subsidiary to double-digit profitability and with finding new markets for its Appleton Electric business, which had been heavily involved in nuclear products.
The printing company must cut costs, re-examine expansion moves and review its international operations, Oppenheimer & Co analyst Edward Atorino said.
"In the short term, it will have to fix problems at its money-losing Stream International (software unit) and look at market share and growth opportunities," Atorino said.

Stream, which provides software-related services for the world's major software publishers and hardware manufacturers, posted a $29 million operating loss last year, excluding restructuring charges. The unit accounted for $1.7 billion of Donnelley's total $6.6 billion revenue, or about 25 percent.

Twenty percent of Donnelley's 1996 revenue came from catalog and newspaper insert printing, 17 percent from magazines, 11 percent from books, including the Bible, and 11 percent from telephone directories.
Davis also will become Donnelley's chairman following a March 27 board meeting, succeeding acting chairman and CEO John Richman. Davis was not available for interviews.
Richman stepped in last October to replace John Walter, who quit to become president and chief operating officer of AT&T Corp.

"It's good they have somebody in place. People like the idea that the issue has been settled," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Rudolf Hokanson. "The management team at Emerson had an excellent reputation."
Donnelley also is the target in a $500 million federal class-action lawsuit alleging racial discrimination based on layoffs, promotions and wages. It has denied the allegations.
R.R. Donnelley's stock rose two to 32-3/8.
